page: Vultr vhf-16c-58gb is a virtual server in the High Frequency Compute family, featuring 16 shared vCPUs mapped from 8 physical Intel x86_64 cores with hyper-threading. It is equipped with 58.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.62 GB per core. Storage is bundled as a 1024 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no dedicated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks place this instance mostly in the average tier. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1250.0 and a multi-core score of 6297.0, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 12970.06. While cached memory bandwidth is strong at 907.89 GB/sec for small blocks, uncached memory bandwidth drops significantly, with large block reads at 24.85 GB/sec and large block writes at 13.66 GB/sec. Static web serving throughput is also on the lower end at 6.08 GB/sec.

The shared CPU allocation presents a performance tradeoff, as resource contention may affect sustained workloads. However, the bundled 1024 GB NVMe SSD and 58.0 GB RAM offer a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads. It is suitable for software compilation, database operations, and moderate web serving where absolute CPU isolation is not critical.
